lines.text: Flip a coin eight times. Will the same side come up three times in a row?
lines.caption: Flip a coin eight times. Will the same side come up three times in a row?

lines.text: It happens almost three times out of four!
lines.caption: It happens almost three times out of four!

lines.text: A fair coin is flipped eight times.
lines.caption: A fair coin is flipped eight times.

lines.text: What is the chance the same side never comes up three times in a row?
lines.caption: What is the chance the same side never comes up three times in a row?

lines.text: Count the good strings, one flip at a time. One flip has two. Two flips have four.
lines.caption: Count the good strings, one flip at a time. One flip has two. Two flips have four.

lines.text: Here's the pattern. Each count is the sum of the two before it!
lines.caption: Here's the pattern. Each count is the sum of the two before it!

lines.text: Six, ten, sixteen, twenty-six, forty-two, sixty-eight!
lines.caption: Six, ten, sixteen, twenty-six, forty-two, sixty-eight!

lines.text: Sixty-eight good strings, out of two hundred fifty-six. That's seventeen over sixty-four, choice D!
lines.caption: Sixty-eight good strings, out of two hundred fifty-six. That's seventeen over sixty-four, choice D!

lines.text: Only about twenty-seven percent. So three in a row is really common!
lines.caption: Only about twenty-seven percent. So three in a row is really common!
